subject: POC acceptance rubric, stretch goals, and ops ownership
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Marino <alex.marino@brightedge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: POC acceptance rubric, stretch goals, and ops ownership

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Wanted to capture the concrete acceptance criteria we discussed and set next steps so the team can line up infra and test harness work. Please review the enclosed draft rubric (attached) and call out anything you'd like tightened up. High-level: we propose a two-tier acceptance approach (required gates + stretch goals).

Required acceptance gates (pass/fail):
- Latency (p95): <= 350 ms on your representative short prompts (see sample workload).
- Throughput: sustain 50 requests/sec with end-to-end p95 latency < 500 ms during a 10-minute ramp test.
- Cost: model config should not exceed $0.0009/token avg (inference cost baseline).
- Quality: top-level functional criteria — intent preservation >= 93% on our shared eval set; hallucination rate <= 2% (manual spot-check).

Stretch goals (nice-to-have, used for ops tuning and final scoring):
- Latency p95 under 250 ms.
- Cost < $0.0006/token with quantized variant.
- Throughput 100 req/sec sustained with autoscaling policy.
- Quality lift: precision on entity extraction > 95% and F1 > 0.88 on edge cases.

Ownership (proposed):
- Redwood runtime config & benchmarking: Priyom Das (pri-ops).
- Monitoring + alerting playbook: Laura Bennett (SLO owner).
- Test harness workload and evaluation script: BrightEdge to provide sample workload; Redwood will adapt harness.

Attachments: brightedge_poc-rubric-v1.xlsx (rubric + measurement sheet); sample-workload-specs.json (prompts + size distribution).

Next steps:
1) Alex to confirm sample workload by Thurs 7/17.
2) Redwood to provision a dedicated test pool and share run-book by 7/21.
3) Joint ramp test week of 7/28; final acceptance run week of 8/4.

If that timeline looks off, flag it and we can compress.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0173

From: Alex Marino <alex.marino@brightedge.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 18:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC acceptance rubric, stretch goals, and ops ownership

Thanks Rishi — the summary is super helpful. A couple of quick notes from our side after the internal huddle:  

- Latency: we can accept p95 <= 350 ms for short prompts, but would like the acceptance to explicitly exclude the 90th+ percentile of long-context prompts (we'll provide the sample set).
- Cost: can you add an allowance for cache-hit adjusted cost? Our production workload has heavy repetition, and effective cost/token will be lower with prefix caching; we may ask to include both raw and cache-adjusted numbers in the rubric.
- Quality: instead of a single 93% intent preservation number, can we split into two buckets — core intents (>=95%) and edge intents (>=88%)?

Also, regarding timeline: the 7/21 run-book is fine, but BrightEdge legal needs a short SOW (1 page) before we sign off on dedicated test capacity. Can you share a draft SOW and a short procurement checklist?

Finally, for stretch goals we think the 100 req/sec is ambitious but makes sense as a stretch — happy to prioritize the latency and cost stretch first.

I attached a short sample workload snapshot (not full set) and flagged prompts that are latency-sensitive.

—Alex
Alex Marino
Head of Data Products, BrightEdge Inc.
alex.marino@brightedge.com | +1 (617) 555-2491
Attachment: brightedge_sample_snapshot.csv

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: POC acceptance rubric, stretch goals, and ops ownership

Laura / Priyom — forwarding Alex's notes. Action items below:  

- Priyom: adjust the rubric to include cache-adjusted cost column and add separate quality buckets (core vs edge intents). Update the spreadsheet and attach estimated cost delta for quantized + cached scenario. Owner: Priyom — due EOD 7/16.
- Laura: draft the 1-page SOW and procurement checklist. Keep the SOW high-level: scope, timeline, point-of-contact, and cancellation terms. Owner: Laura — draft by 7/16 morning so we can share with Alex's legal.
- Me: I'll confirm the exact sample workload files we need and ask BrightEdge for the long-context exclusions.

Also adding a quick ops note — we'll run two ramp patterns: steady-state 50 req/s then spike to 100 req/s for 2 minutes. We should capture p50/p95/p99 latency and CPU/GPU utilization traces; include cost-per-minute for the ramp windows.

I'll follow up with calendar invites for the 7/21 run-book review and the joint ramp test week of 7/28.

Rishi

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Alex Marino <alex.marino@brightedge.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC acceptance rubric, stretch goals, and ops ownership

Alex — thanks for the snapshot and the clarifications. Draft SOW attached (one-pager) and a procurement checklist (internal-facing). Key clarifications we added:  

- Acceptance tests will be run against the sample workload you provide; long-context prompts will be excluded from the latency acceptance gate as requested, but we'll run a separate long-context stress analysis and share the results.
- Cost rows will show raw per-token inference cost and cache-adjusted effective cost (we will document cache hit assumptions).
- Quality buckets: core intents >=95% (required) and edge intents >=88% (required). We left hallucination threshold at <=2% as a required gate.

Attachments: brightedge_sow-1page.pdf, procurement-checklist.txt

Next steps: 
- Alex to confirm the representative workload plus the list of long-context prompts by 7/17.
- Priyom to update rubric + cost sheet by 7/16.
- Rishi to share calendar invites for run-book review (7/21) and ramp test (week of 7/28).

If all good, we'll route the SOW to your legal and aim to have capacity provisioned by 7/21.

Laura Bennett
Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0882
Attachment: brightedge_sow-1page.pdf; procurement-checklist.txt
